unit-m5u5.title: Unit 5 · Lesson 5: Record Division with Two-Digit Divisors
unit-m5u5.source: enVision Topic 5 Student Edition practice pages — dividing by two-digit divisors (Drive)

summary.text: Lesson 5-5 practice pages: recording division with a two-digit divisor, step by step, with remainders and zeros in the quotient, and deciding what a remainder means in a word problem.

why.text: This is the written method she will use for every division from here on, so the steps and the remainder rule need to be solid.

objectives.text: Divide by a two-digit divisor, recording each step
Decide where the first digit of the quotient goes
Find a remainder that is smaller than the divisor
Decide what a remainder means in a word problem

parentNote.text: Built from the lesson 5-5 practice pages in her Unit 5 folder, read for what they ask. The numbers are fresh, not the page's own. The two slips most worth a word are a digit that is too small (so what is left is bigger than the divisor, as in 627 ÷ 29 written as 20 R47) and the remainder written into the quotient (12 R5 as 125). Three word problems cover the three things a remainder can mean: round up for buses, drop it for full flower beds, and the remainder as the answer for apples left over. The page itself asks what a remainder means, so those are marked as from the class material.

nextUp.text: Estimate, then divide, multiply, subtract, bring down, and check.

cards.def:
**Round to numbers that divide easily, so you know about how big the answer should be.**
• 2,486 ÷ 34 is about 2,400 ÷ 30 = 80.
cards.hint: A rough answer catches a wrong digit.

cards.def:
**If the divisor fits into the first two digits, the quotient starts in the tens place. If not, it starts in the ones place.**
• 739 ÷ 31: 31 fits into 73, so the quotient has two digits.
• 517 ÷ 64: 64 does not fit into 51, so it has one digit.
cards.hint: Find the first part the divisor fits into.

cards.def:
**The same four steps as with one-digit divisors, repeated for each digit.**
• Divide: how many times does the divisor fit?
• Multiply, subtract, then bring down the next digit.
cards.hint: D, M, S, B, then again.

cards.def:
**If a subtraction leaves the divisor or more, the digit you wrote is too small.**
• 627 ÷ 29: writing 20 leaves 47, and 47 is more than 29, so it is 21.
cards.hint: What is left must be smaller than the divisor.

cards.def:
**If a brought-down number is smaller than the divisor, write 0 and bring down the next digit.**
• 5,412 ÷ 52 = 104 R4, not 14 R4.
cards.hint: Every digit you bring down gets a digit in the quotient.

cards.def:
**The remainder goes after an R. It is never another digit of the quotient.**
• 845 ÷ 70 = 12 R5, not 125.

**In a story, decide what the remainder means.**
• Round up when everyone must fit (buses).
• Drop it when only full groups count (full flower beds).
• Sometimes the remainder is the answer (apples left over).
cards.hint: Ask: what is the leftover in this story?

cards.def:
**Divisor × quotient + remainder should give back the dividend.**
• 21 × 20 + 17 = 437, so 437 ÷ 21 = 20 R17.

questions.q: In 739 ÷ 31, where does the first digit of the quotient go?
questions.hint: Does 31 fit into 7? Does it fit into 73?
steps: So the first digit goes in the tens place.

ex.main: **The tens place.** 31 is bigger than 7, so start with 73 tens. The quotient has two digits: 23 R26.
ex.tip: Where the first digit goes tells you how many digits the answer has.

questions.q: How many digits will the quotient of 517 ÷ 64 have?
questions.hint: Compare 64 with the first two digits, 51.
steps: 64 is bigger than 51, so it does not fit into 51 tens.

ex.main: **One digit.** 64 does not fit into 51 tens, so the quotient starts in the ones place: 8 R5.
ex.tip: Estimate: 64 × 10 = 640 is more than 517, so the answer is less than 10.

questions.q: A quotient is written 18 R7. What does the R7 tell you?
opts: The answer is 18.7, a little more than 18
There are 7 equal groups in all
7 are left over after the equal groups are made
You need 7 more groups to finish
steps: 18 is the number in each group, or the number of groups.
R7 means 7 are left over that do not make a full group.

ex.main: **7 are left over.** The R stands for remainder: what is left when no more full groups fit.
ex.tip: The remainder is always smaller than the divisor.

questions.hint: Divisor times quotient, then add the remainder.
steps: That is the dividend, so the answer checks out.

ex.main: **21 × 20 + 17 = 437.** Divisor × quotient + remainder gives back the dividend.
ex.tip: Forgetting to add the remainder makes a right answer look wrong.

questions.hint: 23 fits into 85 tens. How many times?
steps: 23 does not fit into 8, so start with 85.
85 ÷ 23 is 3: 3 × 23 = 69, and 85 − 69 = 16. Bring down the 1 to make 161.

ex.main: **37.** Check: 23 × 37 = 851. The wrong answers come from real slips: 36 R23 is one group short, which leaves a remainder too big to keep; 38 is one group too many; 370 is a zero too many.
ex.tip: Each subtraction must leave less than 23.

steps: 27 does not fit into 6, so start with 69.
69 ÷ 27 is 2: 2 × 27 = 54, and 69 − 54 = 15. Bring down the 3 to make 153.

ex.main: **25 R18.** Check: 27 × 25 + 18 = 693. The wrong answers come from real slips: 25 is the remainder left off; 24 R45 is one group short, which leaves a remainder too big to keep; 2,518 is the remainder written into the quotient.
ex.tip: The remainder must be smaller than 27.

questions.hint: 34 does not fit into 24, so start with 248.
steps: 34 does not fit into 24, so start with 248.
248 ÷ 34 is 7: 7 × 34 = 238, and 248 − 238 = 10. Bring down the 6 to make 106.

ex.main: **73 R4.** Check: 34 × 73 + 4 = 2,486. The wrong answers come from real slips: 73 is the remainder left off; 72 R38 is one group short, which leaves a remainder too big to keep; 730 R4 is a zero too many.
ex.tip: Estimate: 2,400 ÷ 30 = 80, so expect a two-digit answer.

questions.hint: 52 fits into 54 once. What happens when you bring down the 1?
steps: 52 does not fit into 5, so start with 54.
54 ÷ 52 is 1: 1 × 52 = 52, and 54 − 52 = 2. Bring down the 1 to make 21.
21 is less than 52, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down the 2 to make 212.

ex.main: **104 R4.** Check: 52 × 104 + 4 = 5,412. The wrong answers come from real slips: 14 R4 is the zero in the quotient skipped; 104 is the remainder left off; 103 R56 is one group short, which leaves a remainder too big to keep.
ex.tip: Every digit you bring down gets a digit in the quotient, even a 0.

questions.hint: Think of 84 tens ÷ 7 tens to start.
steps: 70 does not fit into 8, so start with 84.
84 ÷ 70 is 1: 1 × 70 = 70, and 84 − 70 = 14. Bring down the 5 to make 145.

ex.main: **12 R5.** Check: 70 × 12 + 5 = 845. The wrong answers come from real slips: 125 is the remainder written into the quotient; 11 R75 is one group short, which leaves a remainder too big to keep; 12 is the remainder left off.
ex.tip: Write the remainder after the R; it is not another digit.

questions.q: A school is taking 214 students on a trip. Each bus holds 36 students. How many buses does the school need?
questions.hint: Find 214 ÷ 36. Then ask: can the leftover students stay behind?
steps: The 34 students left over still need a bus.

ex.main: **6 buses.** 214 ÷ 36 = 5 R34, and the 34 left over need a bus too. 5 leaves them behind, 34 is the remainder, not the buses, and "5 R34 buses" is not a number of buses.
ex.tip: When everyone must fit, round the quotient up.

questions.q: A gardener has 500 tulip bulbs and plants 45 in each flower bed. How many beds can she fill completely?
questions.hint: Find 500 ÷ 45. Is the leftover enough for a whole bed?
steps: 5 bulbs cannot fill a bed of 45.

ex.main: **11 beds.** 500 ÷ 45 = 11 R5. The 5 leftover bulbs do not fill a bed, so the answer is 11. 12 rounds up, 5 is the remainder, and 111 writes the remainder in as a digit.
ex.tip: When only full groups count, drop the remainder.

questions.q: A store packs 330 apples into bags of 14. How many apples are left over after it fills as many bags as it can?
questions.hint: Find 330 ÷ 14. Which part of the answer is the leftover?
steps: The question asks for the leftover apples: 8.

ex.main: **8 apples.** 330 ÷ 14 = 23 R8. 23 is the number of bags, 24 rounds up, and 14 is the bag size. Here the remainder IS the answer.
ex.tip: Read the question: it asks for what is left, not how many bags.

questions.q: A coach has 900 stickers to share equally among 38 players. Can each player get 25 stickers?
opts: No, each player can get only 23
Yes, each gets 25 with some left over
Yes, each gets 26 and none are left
No, each player can get only 2

ex.main: **No, only 23 each.** 900 ÷ 38 = 23 R26. For 25 each she would need 38 × 25 = 950 stickers. 2 is the tens digit alone, which loses a place.
ex.tip: Check: 38 × 25 = 950 is more than 900, which says no right away.

questions.q: Max divided 627 ÷ 29 and wrote 20 R47. What should he fix?
opts: Nothing, because 29 × 20 + 47 = 627, so it checks out
47 is bigger than 29, so one more group fits: 21 R18
He should drop the remainder and write just 20
He should start again with a first guess of 29 × 30
questions.hint: Compare the remainder with the divisor.
steps: 47 is bigger than 29, so another group fits.

ex.main: **One more group fits: 21 R18.** His check works out, but a remainder of 47 is more than the divisor, so the ones digit was too small.
ex.tip: If a subtraction leaves the divisor or more, the digit above it is too small.

questions.q: Which division has a quotient of 7 R12?
questions.hint: Try each one: 25 × 7 = 175. Which dividend is 12 more than that?

ex.main: **187 ÷ 25.** 25 × 7 + 12 = 187. 175 forgets the remainder, and 212 and 162 are one group too many and one too few.
ex.tip: Build the dividend: divisor × quotient + remainder.
